chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washa', who said, 'Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr narrated to me, saying, I heard Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) saying'

'Indeed Ali (peace be upon him) is a door from the doors of Guidance. So whoever enters from the door of Ali is a believer, and whoever exits from it is a disbeliever, and whoever does not enter into it nor exits from it is in the class of those for whom Allah has the will (to decide their fate).'

key_terms.بَابٌ: door (metaphor for entry point or authority)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Imam Ali being described as a door of guidance in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the Shia doctrine of 'Wilayah' by positioning Imam Ali as the exclusive gateway to faith, a concept central to the distinction between true belief and disbelief. The tripartite classification highlights that while entry through Ali guarantees iman, those who remain outside this spiritual sphere are not necessarily condemned but remain under Allah's direct prerogative (al-mashi'ah), reflecting the nuance between divine decree and human accountability.
